https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkiy.text: Türkiye to deploy F-16s to Estonia for NATO’s News Türkiye July 26 2026 14:57:56 Türkiye to deploy F-16s to Estonia for NATO’s The Turkish Air Force will once again contribute to NATO ’s Baltic Air Policing mission by deploying five F-16 fighter jets and 76 personnel from the 181st Jet Squadron Command, also known as Panther Squadron, to Amari Air Base in Estonia. The contingent, based at the 8th Main Jet Base Command in the southeastern province of Diyarbakır, will serve from August through November, maintaining round-the-clock quick reaction alert (QRA) duties to respond to potential airspace violations over the Baltic region. Speaking to Turkish state-run Anadolu Agency, before the deployment, a senior official from the command described air policing as a peacetime air defense mission carried out under NATO to safeguard allied airspace. He noted that the Baltic Air Policing mission is specifically designed to protect the airspace of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, which do not operate fighter aircraft of their own. During the deployment, Turkish crews will remain on continuous alert against unidentified aircraft or possible airspace incursions while also participating in joint activities with other NATO allies. First Lt. Özmen, one of the pilots assigned to the mission, said rigorous and continuous training is the key to maintaining the squadron’s high operational standards. He underlined that the success of every fighter sortie depends on the coordinated efforts of maintenance crews, air traffic controllers, planners and support personnel, emphasizing that teamwork is as important as pilot skill. NATO’s Baltic Air Policing mission is a standing peacetime operation that ensures the security of allied airspace through the permanent presence of fighter aircraft and crews on 24/7 quick reaction alert. It has been carried out since Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania joined the alliance in 2004. https://www.dailyecho.co.uk/news/2641372.text: Business Fareham Barnbrook Systems attends Farnborough Airshow for 16th year By William Dalgleish Reporter Share 0 Comments Andrew Barnett, managing director of Barnbrook Systems. (Image: Barnbrook Systems) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A record-breaking year at the Farnborough International Airshow has put a spotlight on the growing importance of global defence and technology. Barnbrook Systems, headquartered in Fareham , marked its 16th consecutive appearance at the airshow by welcoming a record number of visitors from the UK and overseas. Andrew Barnett, managing director at Barnbrook Systems, said: "It was a record year at an airshow which had a very different feel about it. "There was a greater focus than ever on defence and especially upon the application of technology for the rapidly evolving nature of modern warfare. READ MORE: Market traders frustrated over being 'turfed out' during busiest months "It was also telling that many operators, primes and militaries were seeking improved efficiencies to extend the operational life and effectiveness of their platforms amid budgetary pressures despite increasing geo-political instability." The company showcased a range of technologies at its stand, including Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) services, its BlueCube-powered sensing and monitoring technology, and the E:BAG lithium-ion battery fire suppression device developed in partnership with Flair. Mr Barnett, who is also a board member of the Farnborough Aerospace Consortium (FAC), said: "We are now following up on contacts made at the show and business opportunities around the world to support Barnbrook’s strategic growth and support the UK and allied defence infrastructure." Among the visitors to the Barnbrook stand were MPs and representatives from Germany, the US, France, India, and Czechoslovakia. The firm also hosted a reception for the South Central Regional Defence and Security Cluster (SCRDSC), which Mr Barnett chairs. More than 120 delegates attended the SCRDSC breakfast event, held at the FAC stand, to network and explore new partnership opportunities. READ MORE: Dozens of businesses join campaign to protect free-roaming animals Defence Secretary Wes Streeting confirmed at the show that the government's £298b Defence Investment Plan will go ahead, including a £15bn uplift over the next four years. Mr Barnett said: "The Defence Investment Plan is finally out, and with the new government team in place, we are now more hopeful within the defence sector. "Mr Streeting must be prepared to fight the corner of defence and secure even greater investment, which must make its way down the supply chain through prime contractors to SMEs." https://hungarytoday.hu/world-war-i-fall.text: World War I Fallen Honored at Memorial Service in Italy’s Doberdò A memorial service was held Thursday at the Hungarian Chapel (Cappella Ungherese) in Visintini, a village in the municipality of Doberdò del Lago, Italy, to honor the heroes who fell on the Doberdò Front, one of the most horrific battlefields of World War I. The Hungarian Military History Institute and Museum (HIM) shared pictures of the commemoration on its Facebook page. As noted in the post, Colonel Roland Maruzs, commander of the HIM, emphasized in his speech that Doberdò is not merely a barren Italian plateau overlooking the Isonzo Valley, but an eternal symbol of Hungarian military virtue, unimaginable suffering, and steadfast resilience to the very end.” “Let us bow our heads today before the nameless and named heroes of Doberdò! Before those who remained here in foreign soil, and also before those who returned home physically and mentally maimed, yet preserved the purity of their sense of duty in their hearts to the very end. Their memory must not fade, and the greatness of their deeds must shine upon us forever as a torch of loyalty and patriotism,” he said. Peter Ferfoglia, mayor of Doberdò Del Lago, emphasized in his speech that the Hungarian chapel no longer divides but rather brings together and unites nations. He noted that it was very important that cadets also participated in the commemoration, since they are the hope for the future. We must remember the past and look toward the future, for this is the path that, if we walk it together, will lead us toward peace among our peoples,” he said. The commemoration was attended by Colonel Massimiliano Fioretti, representing the Italian Ministry of Defense; Gianfranco Simonit, an Italian local historian and president of the Gruppo Speleologico Carsico; a delegation from the Public Benefit Foundation for Research on the Great War; and cadets from the Károly Kratochvil Military High School and Boarding School. Some of the cadets wore World War I-era uniforms and period equipment, while others wore their school uniforms. All paid their respects to the fallen. The Austro-Hungarian troops defending the Doberdò Plateau along the Italian-Slovenian border consisted predominantly of Hungarian soldiers. The 46th Infantry Regiment from Szeged and the 39th Infantry Regiment from Debrecen defended the hills near Visintini. In January 1918, Emperor Charles IV of Austria and King of Hungary, who was visiting the theater of war, personally intervened to ensure the establishment of a memorial chapel. The Hungarian soldiers began construction of the chapel, which was nearly complete by October; however, due to the collapse of the front, it could not be consecrated. Charles IV visits the joint memorial to the Italian and Hungarian soldiers who fell in the battles along the Isonzo River. Photo: Fortepan / György Széman For decades, the chapel was in a state of disrepair and neglect; it was used as a stable and a storage shed, and then slowly began to crumble. Around the turn of the millennium, the building was saved from ruin through a joint effort by the Isonzo Friendship Association of Gorizia, Italy, and Hungarian civil society organizations. The Széchenyi Scientific Society ultimately undertook the costs of restoring the Hungarian chapel in 2008, considering it important that the memorial site be worthy of commemorating all the heroic fallen in the battles along the Isonzo, while also becoming a European symbol of reconciliation and peace. The renovated chapel was inaugurated by President László Sólyom on May 29, 2009, during the Hungarian Heroes’ Memorial Day, following an ecumenical consecration in honor of Saint Benedict of Nursia, the patron saint of Europe. Following the inauguration, the memorial site became a place of pilgrimage and a symbol of Hungarian military sacrifice.
